name: Colwood

facts.text: Removing a protected tree in Colwood needs a Tree Management Permit under Urban Forest Bylaw No. 1735. You apply online with a Tree Site Plan (five or fewer trees) or a Tree Management Plan, plus photos.
facts.excerpt: If the tree you are planning to remove is a protected tree, you will need to obtain a Tree Management Permit.
facts.note: V2: confirmed; colwood.ca/node/5090 redirects here. The bylaw number is confirmed on https://www.colwood.ca/city-hall/bylaws/1735/urban-forest-bylaw-consolidated. An Amendment No. 3 (Bylaw 1735-03) went to Council for readings on June 9, 2025; whether it was adopted is not confirmed.

facts.text: Colwood protects arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew at 2 m tall or 4 cm in diameter; Douglas-fir, grand fir, bigleaf maple and western redcedar at 30 cm in diameter; any tree over 60 cm in diameter at chest height; and retained, replacement and wildlife trees.
facts.excerpt: Pacific Yew (2m or greater in height OR 4cm or greater in diameter) Douglas Fir (30cm diameter or more)
facts.note: V2: REPLACES the R1b fact 'colwood-protected-30cm', which wrongly said trees of 30 cm or more are protected. The 30 cm threshold applies only to the four conifer and maple species, and other trees are protected only over 60 cm. This confirms the species thresholds in research/areas.json. The 2024 rack card (https://www.colwood.ca/sites/default/files/2024-06/rack-card-urban-forest-bylaw.pdf) also lists trees in environmentally sensitive areas, by creeks or on steep slopes.

facts.text: A Colwood tree permit application needs a Tree Site Plan or Tree Management Plan plus photos; removing more than five protected trees needs a Tree Management Plan by a qualified professional.
facts.excerpt: If you are cutting more than five protected trees, you will need to provide a Tree Management Plan prepared by a qualified professional.
facts.note: V2: the 2017 application PDF URL now redirects to the Tree Permits page; the same wording is confirmed there, so the source was updated. The page also states an application fee; CONTRACT: no $ amounts.

facts.text: Colwood replacement trees go on the same lot: one for each tree when one to five are removed, two for each when more than five are removed. They must be at least 1.5 m tall and native to the Coastal Douglas-fir zone. A per-tree security deposit is refunded after the tree survives a year, or a cash-in-lieu payment applies if trees cannot be planted on the lot.
facts.excerpt: When removing one to five trees, they must be replaced at a 1:1 ratio. When removing more than five trees, they must be replaced at a 2:1 ratio.
facts.note: V2: new; closes the R1b gap on the replacement ratio. The page lists Coastal Douglas-fir zone natives (arbutus, grand fir, red alder, black cottonwood, shore pine, western redcedar, bigleaf maple, Pacific crab apple, western white pine, Douglas-fir, Pacific dogwood, western hemlock, Garry oak, western yew). CONTRACT: no $ amounts.

facts.text: Colwood needs no permit for pruning done to sound arboricultural practice. That does not cover lift pruning below a 50% live crown ratio, removing more than 25% of the crown in one season, topping, or cutting a structural root in the critical root zone. Hedges (five or more trees under 5 m tall planted 1.25 m apart) can be pruned or removed without a permit.
facts.excerpt: removal of more than 25% of the crown in one season, topping, or pruning or removal of a structural root within the critical root zone.
facts.note: V2: new; closes the R1b gap on pruning and hedge exemptions.

facts.text: Colwood's Hillside development permit guidelines (posted OCP text marked DRAFT) say to avoid tree removal on steep slopes, re-vegetate exposed soil on steep slopes with plants native to the Coastal Douglas-fir zone, avoid fast-growing non-native plants for holding soil, and keep windfirm treed buffers between lots.
facts.sourceTitle: 22. Hillside Environmental DPA (Colwood OCP, DRAFT text)
facts.excerpt: Avoid tree removal on steep slopes. Trees intercept precipitation and reduce stormwater runoff volumes, protect soils from erosion
facts.note: V2: Correction: 'Development on slopes over 30% must be avoided' is NOT in this PDF, so it was removed from the text. The rest is confirmed (guidelines 22.1 b, c, g, h, i). The PDF carries a DRAFT watermark. The consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 1700 Part D is hosted on colwood.civicweb.net, which this session's network refused, so the wording in force is unconfirmed.

facts.text: Colwood's riparian and marine-shoreline development permit guidelines (posted OCP text marked DRAFT) treat the shoreline as running from the low-tide mark to 11 m above sea level. They set a permanent natural buffer of at least 30 m upland from the natural boundary, do not support shoreline hardening, and keep new structures, including docks, out of the Esquimalt Lagoon Migratory Bird Sanctuary, which includes 100 m from the lagoon's natural boundary.
facts.sourceTitle: 20. Riparian Areas and Marine Shorelines Environmental DPA (Colwood OCP, DRAFT text)
facts.excerpt: New structures, including docks, may not be located within the Esquimalt Lagoon Migratory Bird Sanctuary which includes 100 m from the present natural boundary of the Lagoon.
facts.note: V2: confirmed against the PDF, and the 30 m buffer was added (s.20.2 a). The PDF is watermarked DRAFT. Council held a public hearing on Feb 27, 2025 on 'OCP No. 1700, Amendment No. 10 (Environmental Development Permit Area)', which rewrote the riparian guidelines (https://www.colwood.ca/news/notice-public-hearing-environmental-development-permit-areas). The in-force text on colwood.civicweb.net could not be reached. Use only with 'check with the City'.

facts.text: Colwood's drier sites are Garry oak country; those ecosystems hold a high share of the region's rare species and fall under its Sensitive Ecosystems guidelines.
facts.sourceTitle: 21. Sensitive Ecosystems Environmental DPA (Colwood OCP, DRAFT text)
facts.excerpt: Garry oak ecosystems dominate other drier areas of Colwood
facts.note: V2 UNVERIFIED: the PDF was fetched (2 pages, DRAFT), but neither the excerpt nor any Garry oak wording appears in it. The full Part D on colwood.civicweb.net was unreachable. Do not publish this as a City statement. A safe alternative is colwood-protected-trees (Garry oak protected from 2 m / 4 cm).

facts.text: Open burning is not allowed in Colwood at any time: no open yard, beach, camp, land-clearing, demolition or construction-waste fires, so yard debris is chipped or hauled (the City runs a Branch Drop Off). Factory-made outdoor wood-burning appliances with a firebox no larger than 24 by 24 inches are allowed at least 20 ft from buildings, fences, property lines and vegetation, except when the fire rating is High or Extreme.
facts.excerpt: The City of Colwood prohibits all open yard fires, beach fires and camp fires as well as land clearing, demolition and construction waste fires.
facts.note: V2: colwood.ca/node/140 now returns 'Access Denied'; the current page is Community Services > Safety > Fire. Correction: 'certified' appliances changed to the page's wording, 'specifically manufactured for this purpose - no homemade devices'. Outdoor Burning Restriction and Regulation Bylaw No. 931, 2007.

facts.text: Colwood's Pesticide Use Bylaw generally bars pesticides on lawns, trees, shrubs, flowers and other ornamental plants at homes, duplexes, townhouses, apartments and condominiums. Listed lower-risk products are allowed without a permit, and a permit may be issued for invasive species, noxious weeds or infestations that threaten a sensitive ecosystem. The bylaw does not apply to commercial, institutional or industrial properties.
facts.excerpt: Pesticide use is generally NOT permitted on lawns and gardens in Colwood
facts.note: V2: new. Same page, verbatim: 'It does not apply to: ... Commercial, institutional, or industrial properties.' Permits go through Colwood Parks (250-474-4133). The page lists a maximum fine; CONTRACT: no $ amounts.

facts.text: In Colwood, the property owner maintains the boulevard between the lot and the street or sidewalk, keeping grass trimmed and litter cleared. The City asks owners to contact it before changing a boulevard, since plantings or structures are usually not possible over underground utilities.
facts.excerpt: maintenance of the boulevard between your property and the street or sidewalk in Colwood is the responsibility of the property owner.
facts.note: V2: new. The page cites the Traffic and Highways Bylaw.

facts.text: Colwood's Branch Drop Off accepts Scotch broom, English ivy, English holly, Himalayan blackberry, English hawthorn and periwinkle. The City flags poison hemlock, giant hogweed, Japanese knotweed and blessed milk thistle as common culprits.
facts.excerpt: Know what you can bring to Colwood Branch Drop Off: We CAN ACCEPT: Scotch Broom, English Ivy, English Holly, Himalayan Blackberry, English Hawthorn and Periwinkle.
facts.note: V2: new. Infestations are reported to the Coastal Invasive Species Committee (info@coastalisc.com).

facts.text: Colwood offers free FireSmart home assessments to residents through a FireSmart coordinator, with the focus on the Home Ignition Zone, the 30 m around a home.
facts.excerpt: The area within 30 metres of your home is called the Home Ignition Zone.
facts.note: V2: new; closes the R1b gap on a wildfire program.

facts.text: In Colwood, removing more than 200 cubic metres of soil or rock off site needs a Blasting Permit and a Soil Deposit Permit (Blasting Bylaw No. 272). Blasters must notify everyone within 300 m, and blasting is limited to Monday-Thursday 8:30 am-4 pm and Friday 8:30 am-3 pm, with none on weekends or holidays.
facts.sourceTitle: Blasting & Dust Control - City of Colwood
facts.excerpt: If a company or developer intends to remove soil and/or rock off site that exceeds 200 cubic meters, a Blasting Permit and Soil Deposit Permit are required

facts.text: Royal Bay, Colwood's fastest-growing neighbourhood, has a century-long history as a gravel operation that was one of the region's largest industrial sites, so many yards there are new builds on former pit land.
facts.excerpt: The area has a century-long history as a gravel operation that was one of the region's largest industrial sites and major employers.
facts.note: V2: colwood.ca/node/6830 now returns 404, so the source is now the Neighbourhoods page. Correction: removed '1910 to 2009' and the 'Mine Reclamation Plan' wording, which the current page does not state. 'New builds on former pit land' is our framing; the soil type is not stated by the City.

facts.text: Esquimalt Lagoon is a federally designated Migratory Bird Sanctuary managed by the Canadian Wildlife Service, bordered by some of the oldest coastal Douglas-fir forest left in the Victoria area. Waterfront yards nearby sit beside protected habitat.
facts.excerpt: The lagoon is also bordered by some of the oldest coastal Douglas fir forest remaining in the Victoria area.
facts.note: V2: the federal page (canada.ca) is outside this session's network, so the source is now the CRD page. Same page, verbatim: 'a federally designated Migratory Bird Sanctuary managed by the Canadian Wildlife Service'. Correction: removed the 1931 date and 'surrounding 100 m of land', which were not confirmed (100 m appears only in Colwood's DRAFT DPA text; see colwood-shoreline-lagoon-dpa).
